text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose modestly today, continuing a sharp rebound from early last week—it's up nearly 12% since November 6th—but the gain today was tiny. The backdrop is a tightening balance in the refining business: refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, and heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year, which typically supports margins for refiners that make diesel and heating oil. However, that strength is being tempered by rising crude supply globally—Russian output has recovered, pushing the market into surplus—which puts downward pressure on the fuel margins refiners depend on.

The two-week decline of 6.8% overall reflects this tension: strong heating-oil-driven demand is fighting against a glut of crude coming back online. Refiners benefit when they can turn cheap crude into expensive refined products, but that spread narrows when crude supplies flood the market faster than demand for refined fuels can absorb them.
